neighbours.label: the kind of school someone attended (a Catholic / private / international / coeducational [school])
fire: She grew up in Lyon and attended a private girls' school near the river.
He was educated at an independent boarding school in Kent.
The family moved to Dubai, where the children enrolled in an international school.
As a boy he attended a Jesuit secondary school in Dublin.
She later taught chemistry at a selective grammar school in Birmingham.
Their son goes to a small Montessori school across town.
After the war she was sent to a Catholic convent school in Quebec.
He spent six years at an elite prep school before going to Yale.
quiet: She grew up in Lyon and worked at a private bank near the river.
He was treated at an independent clinic in Kent.
The family moved to Dubai, where the children joined an international football club.
As a boy he attended a Jesuit church in Dublin every Sunday.
She later worked as a chemist at a pharmaceutical firm in Birmingham.
Their son goes to a small judo club across town.
After the war she was sent to work at a Catholic hospital in Quebec.
He spent six years at an elite law firm before going to Yale.

notes: Card: international school, coeducational school, educated [at], attended a [Catholic] high school, grammar schools [and] faith schools. + pole output suppresses school/prep/grammar.
